summary: This defines the MarketProduct class, the domain object for the farmers' market application: a single item on a vendor's table, described by its name, vendor, price, category, season, and whether it is organic. Every stream exercise in this chapter processes lists of these objects.

lines.text: Each field is both private and final, so a MarketProduct's data is set once at construction and can never change afterward. Immutable objects like this are exactly what streams prefer, since nothing can quietly rewrite an item mid-pipeline.

lines.code: public MarketProduct(String name, String vendor, double price, String category, String season, boolean organic) {
lines.text: The constructor is the only way to populate the object, so every product must be described completely up front. Watch the order of the arguments when you create one — name and vendor are both Strings, and the compiler cannot tell you that you swapped them.
The parameter and the field share the name `name`, so `this.name` is needed to say "the field belonging to this object" rather than the parameter.
Java convention names a boolean getter `isOrganic` rather than `getOrganic`, which reads naturally in stream filters later in the chapter.

The odd-looking `'\''` is a single-quote character, escaped because a bare quote would end the character literal. It wraps the text values in quotes so printed output clearly shows where each String begins and ends.
Overriding toString means printing a MarketProduct — or a whole list of them — shows readable field values instead of a class name and hash code, which makes debugging stream results far easier.
